articles.title: Former US officials call on 2028 candidates to denounce Biden’s Gaza policy
articles.summary: Biden-era officials who quit over Gaza urge Democratic candidates for next presidential race to denounce the policy.
articles.body:
United States officials who had resigned from former President Joe Biden’s administration due to his policy on Gaza have called on potential Democratic candidates for the 2028 presidential race to denounce that policy.

In a joint statement titled “Gaza Resignees” published on Wednesday, 12 former officials who had quit between late 2023 and 2024 said they had resigned from their service to the US government over its “illegal and unconditional support for Israel’s actions in Gaza”.

“The most basic level of accountability, the most minimal level of consequences, is to ensure that those who have wreaked so much harm from within the highest levels of our Government cannot return to it,” the statement read.

“We call on candidates for the 2028 Presidential Nomination to commit to not hire any administration official directly responsible for enabling Israel’s military actions in Gaza,” it added.

Several rights groups, experts, scholars and United Nations inquiries have assessed that Israel’s devastating war on Gaza amounts to genocide.

Since October 2023, Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has killed at least 74,564 Palestinians and injured at least 175,770, according to Palestinian health authorities.

The Biden administration, which governed from 2021-2024, has faced pushback and condemnation from progressive lawmakers and activist groups since the war began.

US Representative Rashida Tlaib and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani have opposed the US’s ongoing support for ‌Israel, which has continued since President Donald Trump was re-elected last year.

In advance of the 2028 election, the former officials said several “architects” of Biden’s Gaza policy were now “whitewashing their own roles in enabling genocide”.

“When faced with the opportunity to stand up in defense of our laws, they not only stayed silent, but worked resolutely in pursuit of illegal and wrongful ends in violation of both US and international law,” they said, adding that many of those same officials were now pursuing a path back into policymaking.

The statement called on Democratic candidates for the 2028 presidential race to pledge to three oaths, including to uphold the Constitution and pursue the national interest of the US, and to acknowledge the US’s complicity in Israel’s genocide in Gaza through arms, funding and diplomatic backing.

The third oath urged the nominees to pledge to commit to building an administration that reflects US interests and creates “no space” for those who were an “architect, leader, defender, or key enabler, of the US policies of unconditional support to Israel that constitute complicity in a genocide”.

articles.title: Sixty police officers recruited for new Bee Network unit
articles.summary: Some 60 more officers will be deployed across Manchester's Bee Network to make travel safer.
articles.body:
Sixty police officer have been recruited to patrol Greater Manchester's trams and buses.

The new Transport Policing and Crime Command has been created to tackle crime and antisocial behaviour on the Bee Network.

The new squad will deliver a "significant increase" in visible policing and enforcement across the transport network, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said.

The dedicated unit, which will also cover the city's active travel routes and roads, has been formed with funding from the Mayor of Greater Manchester's budget.

It will be supported by control centre staff at GMP and Transport for Greater Manchester, which has access to CCTV cameras across bus stations, interchanges, tram stops and train stations.

Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said the aim was to "make the roads and public transport among the safest in the UK".

Bev Craig, Mayor of Greater Manchester said the move would "bring together up to 300 police and safety officers, with high-profile patrols across our roads and the Bee Network".

She added: "It means a stronger presence in our communities and faster action when people need help."

The unit would also "crack down on dangerous driving to reduce the number of deaths and serious injuries on our roads", she said.

articles.title: ‘Economic incentives are limited’: What does Russia really offer Africa?
articles.summary: African nations weigh political incentives as Moscow offers limited economic benefits compared with China and the West.
articles.body:
In 2019, I travelled to Berengo Palace, outside Bangui, to interview Russian mercenaries.

Once the home of Jean-Bedel Bokassa, the Central African Republic’s self-crowned emperor, it was now occupied by fighters from the Wagner Group. One of the first things they told me was not about the country they had come to defend, but the country they had left.

Seven years later, Wagner’s founder, Yevgeny Prigozhin, is dead.

In the Sahel, Wagner has given way to Africa Corps, controlled by Russia’s Ministry of Defence. Moscow is fighting a war in Ukraine, where Africans have been recruited, some under false pretences. An investigation by Journalists for Justice documented 502 African deaths by June 2026.

In Douala, Cameroon, I met Mama Regina, her eyes bloodshot as she held back tears. Her son Moses had gone to Russia to fight. His portrait hung on the wall.

“So handsome,” she whispered. Like so many families, she is waiting for his body. Once again, Africans are mourning men lost in someone else’s war on another continent far away from home.

In grief, some have turned to a small but growing Russian Orthodox church. Its Cameroonian pastor was trained in St Petersburg. He says he is here to preach the “good news”.

African leaders are gathering in Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit . In 2019, 43 African heads of state or government attended the first summit in Sochi.

In St Petersburg in 2023, after Russia invaded Ukraine, only 17 heads of state came. Putin offered free grain to six African countries, which Russia later delivered. This year, the Kremlin expects delegations from 48 countries, including 22 heads of state.

“The economic incentives to go for the Russia summit are much more limited,” says Beverly Ochieng, a Dakar-based analyst.

Compared with United States-Africa and China-Africa summits, she says, Moscow offers fewer large investment commitments.

“The political incentives for attending are the primary reasons why these countries are there.”

For the military governments of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, Russia offers something more immediate: Support to remain in power.

France was pushed out; Russia stepped in. Yet armed groups continue to attack, and Human Rights Watch has accused Africa Corps forces in Mali of killing civilians and torturing detainees.

The Soviet Union trained generations of African officers, politicians and students during decolonisation.

Ochieng learned Russian at the embassy in Kenya. Moscow, she says, can still play the card of “we didn’t colonise you.”

But Russia is facing Western sanctions and looking for economic opportunities in its relationship with African nations.

In Mali, construction has begun on a gold refinery backed by Russia’s Yadran Group; the Malian state holds a 62-percent stake. In Guinea, Russian aluminium giant Rusal operates bauxite mines and an alumina plant. In Niger, Rosatom subsidiaries are discussing uranium projects with the government, after the takeover of a mine formerly operated by France’s Orano. A separate attempt to sell existing uranium stockpiles remains in dispute.

Earlier this month, Putin said Russia’s aim was not to “steal something from Africa” but to “develop together”.

Russia’s trade with Africa was about $28bn in 2025, compared with China’s $348bn. The European Union exchanged nearly 355 billion euros ($395bn) in goods with Africa in 2024.

Sergey Eledinov, a former Russian officer and security analyst, sees a trap in Russia’s military bargain in Africa. By securing governments, Moscow may give them room to look elsewhere. “Survival doesn’t create loyalty,” he says. “It creates options.”

Ochieng also cautions against mistaking Russian flags at demonstrations for widespread support. They do not mean “all Africans are just sitting around being pro-Russia,” she said.

For Moscow, she says, the summit is a chance to demonstrate its continued “political relevance”, even if the West increasingly regards it as a pariah state.

articles.title: King tides inundate streets and flood homes  along both U.S. coasts
articles.summary: King tides have inundated parts of both U.S. coasts, flooding streets and sending seawater into homes and businesses in beach communities in California, Florida and the Carolinas.
articles.body: HUNTINGTON BEACH, Calif. — King tides have inundated parts of both U.S. coasts, flooding streets and sending seawater into homes and businesses in beach communities in California, Florida and the Carolinas. The tides began with the full moon earlier this week and could cause flooding in some areas into the weekend, forecasters said. King tides are caused by the gravitational pull and alignments of the Earth, moon, and sun. They can occur several times a year and last several days. This week’s king tides have been exacerbated by additional factors, forecasters said Wednesday. In Florida, strong high pressure to the north and low pressure over the Caribbean were causing increased swells, Chris Fisher, a National Weather Service meteorologist in Miami, said. Along the California coast, the ongoing super El Niño has warmed the ocean, leading to an increased volume of seawater. Another factor was the occurrence of Kelvin waves, a series of pulses of warm water that lift the sea level, said Roger Gass, a meteorologist with the weather service’s Bay Area forecast office in Monterey. This week’s king tides, like their name, have definitely been noticeable. Residents didn’t need a beach to see the ocean. The ocean came to them. In Southern California, Stacey Frederick snapped photos and videos of people walking in knee-deep water and paddleboarding on the Pacific Coast Highway outside a coffee shop where she works as rising tides pushed water ashore. Officials shut down traffic on a flooded portion of the four-lane highway, which winds from Orange County up through California. King tides aren’t new, yet this was unusual, Frederick said. “It floods a little bit, but never to this point,” said Frederick, 38, who has lived in Huntington Beach for five years. Record high tides were set this week in Santa Barbara, San Pedro, San Diego and nearby La Jolla, according to the weather service. In Sunset Beach, the water washed over the three layers of sandbags that Lorraine Friedman, 75, had stacked inside her garage and on the small patio outside her studio apartment. She has lived in the seaside community for nearly three decades and her apartment has flooded only once before, some 20 years ago. “This is the second day I’ve been flooded — two days — and tomorrow I’ll get flooded again,” she said Wednesday. In the northern part of the state, minor flooding was expected through Saturday in low-lying areas along shorelines and tidal waterways during peak high tides, the weather service said. Gass said the coastal flooding generally occurred within 1 1/2 hours before and after high tides, which are peaking 1.9 feet (about a half-meter) above normal in Northern California. Most of Florida’s Atlantic coast was under flood warnings through early Friday. Street flooding also was reported in South Carolina coastal cities, including Charleston and Myrtle Beach, and rip currents were possible as far north as North Carolina’s Outer Banks. “It’s been a rough beach week,” Fisher said. “We’ve had a high risk of rip currents and some high surf out there. The beach conditions are going to continue to be rough through the weekend. It’s been a good week to stay out of the water and stay away from the beaches.” In Fort Lauderdale, Florida, getting to the multiple waterfront venues at what’s billed as the world’s largest-in-water boat show was tricky, requiring driving through flooded streets next to marinas, hotels and convention centers. Virginia Key, a barrier island in Miami, saw its highest king tide and the third-highest water level since records were first kept going back three decades, Fisher said. “The only times we’ve seen higher was during hurricanes,” Fisher said. “It’s historical from a king tide perspective.”

articles.title: A customer booked a Mahindra XUV700 in 2022 but never received the SUV; four years later, a consumer commission has ordered Mahindra and its dealer to refund the booking amount with interest and pay Rs 62,000
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Haryana has held Mahindra & Mahindra and its authorised dealer guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Haryana has held Mahindra & Mahindra and its authorised dealer guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice after they failed to deliver a booked SUV or refund the advance payment. The commission directed them to refund Rs 21,000 with interest, pay Rs 51,000 as compensation and Rs 11,000 in litigation expenses.In its October 7, 2026, order, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Yamuna Nagar, at Jagadhri, held the dealer and manufacturer jointly and severally liable, directing them to comply within 45 days.Booked Mahindra XUV700 never deliveredAccording to the commission order, the customer booked a Mahindra XUV700 diesel automatic in Everest White on February 8, 2022, and paid Rs 21,000 as advance booking money. He was assured that the vehicle would be delivered within six to eight months.When he contacted the dealer in October 2022, after waiting nine months, he was told to wait another month. In November, he was again assured that delivery would happen soon.But in December 2022, the customer checked the vehicle’s booking status online and was surprised to find it marked as invoiced or sold. He alleged that the vehicle booked for him had been sold to someone else. When he questioned the dealer, he was not given a satisfactory answer and was asked to wait longer.The customer also lodged a complaint with the manufacturer through its toll-free number. He said the grievance was registered, but the issue remained unresolved. The SUV was never delivered, and the booking amount was not returned, prompting him to approach the commission in February 2025.However, the dealer denied promising delivery within six to eight months, claiming its staff had tried to contact the customer several times but received no response, so the SUV was allotted to the next person in line. It also denied receiving any extra money. Mahindra & Mahindra said the dealer was a separate entity responsible for the sale and claimed the customer had cancelled the booking, making him ineligible for relief.Commission’s findingThe bench comprising president Rajbir Singh and members Jasvinder Singh and Suman Rana found that the dealer and manufacturer gave contradictory explanations about who received the booking amount and why the SUV was not delivered.The commission observed that “the opponents are self contradictory” in their claims about the payment and the customer’s alleged cancellation of the booking.It noted that neither side produced evidence to show that the customer had been contacted about delivery or had cancelled the booking. The commission also found no proof that the booking amount had been refunded or that the customer was informed the SUV had been allotted to someone else.The bench said the dealer and manufacturer could not escape liability by blaming each other.It observed that “it is the prime duty of opponents to ensure the delivery of the booked vehicle within time to the consumer/customer”. Holding both guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, the commission said their failure to deliver the SUV, refund the booking amount or resolve the grievance had caused the customer mental agony and harassment.Final orderThe commission allowed the complaint and directed the dealer and manufacturer, jointly and severally, to:Refund the Rs 21,000 booking amount with 9 percent annual interest from the date the complaint was filed until payment.Pay Rs 51,000 as compensation for the harassment and inconvenience caused.Pay Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses.The order said the parties must comply within 45 days. If they fail to do so, the amounts awarded under the compensation and litigation-expense heads will carry 12 percent annual interest from the date of filing the complaint until realisation.

articles.title: He’s styled everyone from Rihanna to Naomi Campbell. Carlos Nazario’s first book isn’t what you might expect
articles.summary: The celebrated stylist, and newly announced editor in chief of Wonderland magazine, feels a unique mission to try to change perceptions of who and what is celebrated in fashion.
articles.body: If you were to put together a time capsule that might reflect what life feels like amid the chaos of the 2020s, what would you choose to include? Which artists and subjects — which bodies or voices — would you feature? And would you have the confidence to even trust yourself with such an ambitious project to begin with? These are questions that Carlos Nazario knows all too well, having grappled with them extensively while working on his first-ever book, “Silver Lining,” an ambitious aesthetic adventure through the zeitgeist as Nazario both sees it and wants it to be seen. The celebrated 38-year-old stylist said he felt an urgent pull to produce something substantial to document this moment in the world — an era in which he feels a unique sense that he is living through history and everything that word implies. But in keeping with Nazario’s reputation for daring, even ground-breaking work, this couldn’t be just any fashion book. It needed to send a message — in Nazario’s voice — to future generations. “What I wanted to do was to leave a document that suggested that not everyone thinks that way and that there are people who look different and think different and see different, and they’re no less sophisticated, and they’re no less important, and it shouldn’t be treated with any less respect,” Nazario said. “I hope that people can look back on this and think, ‘Oh, wow, that was the start of that,’ or ‘Oh, that looks really different than I thought 2026 looked like.’” As the newly announced editor in chief of the British fashion title Wonderland, (and contributing style director for Vogue and style director at large for Harper’s Bazaar US before that), Nazario speaks the language of a magazine fluently. His work reflects both a lived-in reality — Nazario, who is Afro-Latino, often champions diverse models — but still plays with fantasy and mythology, as evident in his otherworldly shoot with photographer Tyler Mitchell at the Texas Southern Border to mark the country’s semiquincentennial. He’s styled everyone from Rihanna to Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, notably dressing the Democrat for a 2020 Vanity Fair cover in a custom-made white suit (a nod to the suffragettes) that was designed by a Black man from her congressional district. That was soon after Nazario had dressed Lizzo and Naomi Campbell for Vogue, becoming the first Black stylist to style one of the magazine’s covers since its founding more than a century prior. “The fashion industry can’t seem to get enough of Carlos Nazario,” New York magazine’s The Cut declared in a 2021 profile celebrating the staggering 14 covers he produced in a single year. But as Nazario’s career was taking off, he felt conflicted. The new decade had begun with a deadly pandemic and racial justice movement, which had each morphed into dizzying culture wars mined by political actors seeking power. It felt like a whirlwind. At the time, Nazario was unable even to enjoy his history-making work at Vogue. Instead, he felt angry that it had taken so long for a Black person to be chosen for the opportunity to begin with. The 2021 death of his friend and industry peer Virgil Abloh, the acclaimed menswear designer for Louis Vuitton and founder of streetwear brand Off-White, was another push Nazario needed make the shift to editor of his own work. “All of those things happening at once is really what catapulted me into saying, ‘OK, I have to lock in. I have to make this thing, and maybe it’s OK if it’s not perfect,’” Nazario recalled. “I think that fear of imperfection or failure is a lot of times what prevents us from starting or finishing things.” But although afraid, Nazario wanted to be bold. A book, rather than a magazine, felt like a “more permanent…complete thought,” and a form befitting the deep questions Nazario wanted to tackle. “I didn’t want people to think about this like another stylist making a magazine,” he said. “The content felt way more serious and way more urgent, and certainly covered topics that I wouldn’t have felt comfortable doing so in mainstream magazines.” Stretching across more than 300 pages, and containing various pieces from Nazario and collaborators, “Silver Lining” is indeed an ambitious work. It enjoys the free-wheeling sprit of a fashion or literary magazine, but with the permanence and heft of a prized coffee table tome. Themes of race and the corporeal form echo throughout the book. Luis Alberto Rodriguez’s gorgeous black-and-white photos examining the beauty and varying body types of Black men, are followed immediately by an essay by Darnell L. Moore in which the writer and activist navigates memories of his own body, Blackness and sexuality. Nazario is interested in questions of gender, too. In one project, he and photographer Pieter Hugo traveled to India to shoot a series of sensitive portraits of hijras, a community of third-gender people in South Asia with a semi-sacred status. There is also a striking series by the South London photographer Gabriel Moses, “Bureau of Imagination,” in which models seem to emerge from dark, pop-art canvases, like painted figurines out to reclaim their autonomy. Then there’s the series of inspired conversations between models Alex Consani and Paloma Elsesser, singer Erykah Badu and video artist Arthur Jafa, photographer Ming Smith and musician Solange Knowles — all friends and confidantes of Nazario’s in what can be a ruthless industry. A number of his peers unsurprisingly showed their support for Nazario at his “Silver Lining” launch parties at the boutique Dover Street Market in both New York and Paris leading up to the book’s release. Frequently, though, Nazario pulls us back into the reality of our moment. In “Red Pill, Blue Pill,” the French-Swiss photographer Thaddé Comar captures portraits of rallygoers in the heated 2024 election season — a time in which a comedian sparked outrage by denigrating Puerto Rico as a “floating island of garbage” at one such Trump rally. Then, in “Los Borinqueños,” Oliver Hadlee Pearch and Nazario takes us to that island to spend time with young Puerto Ricans, including the island-born model Joan Smalls, all posed with great dignity and beauty in barber shops, in bed or among nature. The heart of “Silver Lining” can be found halfway through the book in a deeply felt and intimate conversation between Nazario and his own grandmother, Efna Plaza-Merritt, whom Nazario once had pose for the cover of Vogue Italia, wearing Prada, no less. The pair recall how Plaza-Merritt helped raise her grandson, how her anti-gay bigotry came to slowly be replaced by total acceptance and how she continues to struggle with body image issues as an older woman. Some of her dysmorphia comes from her upbringing and identity as a Black woman, but other parts of it have been taught to her by a fashion industry that her grandson is now firmly part of. But this is where Nazario feels a unique mission in his role in the fashion vanguard to try to change perceptions of who and what is celebrated. His photos of his grandmother, for example, shine with an ethereal radiance that transforms the lines in her face and hands into markers celebrating her life and impact. And if beauty standards are going to change, Nazario wants to help drive the conversation from the position of power he enjoys. He recalls the 2011 Chris Brown song “Look At Me Now” in which the singer remarked, “I don’t see how you can hate from outside of the club. You can’t even get in.” That’s an ethos that mirrors what Nazario believes has been among the few silver linings to come from this contentious climate: a growing awareness of what we owe to each other and to the world. “The biggest silver lining we’re experiencing and starting to accept is that we all have to live in this world together,” Nazario said. “We all have a very important responsibility to contribute to the world in whatever format it is.”

articles.title: Fire briefly triggers emergency at South Carolina lab on former nuclear weapons site
articles.summary: A fire at a national lab in South Carolina that is in a complex where key parts for nuclear bombs were once made, triggered an emergency declaration Wednesday that shut down incoming traffic and restricted air and rail service in the area.
articles.body: A fire at a national lab in South Carolina that is in a complex where key parts for nuclear bombs were once made, triggered an emergency declaration Wednesday that shut down incoming traffic and restricted air and rail service in the area. The fire at the Savannah River National Laboratory on the U.S. Department of Energy’s Savannah River Site was extinguished by Wednesday night and the site returned to normal operations. No detectable levels of contamination were found, according to a Savannah River Site statement. The Savannah River Site is a massive complex where the federal government once produced materials used in nuclear weapons, primarily tritium and plutonium-239. The lab is in its northwest corner, near the edge of the site. The site was opened in the early 1950s as the Cold War was heating up. Today it is used for environmental stewardship and cleanup, along with nuclear waste management and disposition of nuclear materials, according to the U.S. Department of Energy. The lab currently does experiments with nuclear materials and also does processing work with radioactive material, including operating a facility for radioisotope recovery from used nuclear fuel, said Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety at the Union of Concerned Scientists. Lyman said it is reassuring that officials said there has been no off-site contamination, noting that there is a buffer zone between most of the facilities and the public areas. But if you have a fire where there is radioactive material, “you need to take extreme precautions because of the potential dispersal of that material and the potential for contamination, potential for the public to be exposed,” he said. The emergency declaration put out Wednesday is the second-highest of three categories of emergencies at the site and indicates “something more serious has occurred,” according to the site’s community preparedness information. The emergency declaration ended Wednesday night after the fire was extinguished.

articles.title: Wang Fuk Court: Hong Kong leader John Lee apologises for deadly high-rise fire at Tai Po
articles.summary: The massive blaze at Wang Fuk Court in November 2025 was the deadliest the city had seen in decades.
articles.body:
The chief executive of Hong Kong, John Lee, has apologised for a massive fire that ripped through an apartment complex last year and killed 168 people.

Speaking at a press conference, Lee promised major reforms to government departments to ensure such an incident would not happen again.

A report by an independent committee, released by the government at the press conference, found that the fire was caused by "misconduct" by the private sector as well as "decades of failure" by government bodies.

The massive blaze at Wang Fuk Court in November 2025 was the deadliest the city had seen in decades. Dozens of people have been arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, fraud or corruption.

At the start of the press conference on Thursday, John Lee said he was "deeply sorrowful" about the fire and that on behalf of his government, "I apologise to the victims as well as the city's residents".

He then stood up and bowed, along with several top officials.

Later he announced that the city's housing secretary Winnie Ho had resigned to take accountability for the fire.

The independent committee's report found that the fire was most likely caused by a "glowing source, likely a cigarette" which ignited "paper materials" at the apartment complex, which was undergoing extensive renovation at the time.

Officials have said the government may start using AI and drones with infra-red cameras to detect and identify smokers on construction sites.

The report also found that the construction companies in charge of the renovation used sub-standard building materials and had unsafe procedures.

This included using scaffolding nets that were not fire retardant and covering up windows with inflammable foam boards for a prolonged period of time.

The companies had also used fake information in paperwork to "feign compliance" with regulators' rules, according to the report.

The committee said the main contractor and consultant for the renovation, as well as several individuals associated with the project, deserved "the most severe criticisms" for the fire.

But had the various government departments involved in the project possessed a "sense of crisis" and "paid sufficient heed" to the possibility of misconduct, it added, such behaviour as well as the fire hazards at Wang Fuk Court could have been rectified.

The report also said there were "widespread, systematic and long-standing" practices in the construction sector that were "unlawful and dubious". There was also bid-rigging and other misconduct by various parties, including some who had connections with local mafias, it said.

Lee said that the various government bodies involved in the case would be investigated, and that a unit in the housing bureau which conducts independent checks would be replaced.

Lee also promised to crack down on bid-rigging, including criminalising the practice, and introduce long jail terms and heavy fines.

Built in the 1980s, Wang Fuk Court in Hong Kong's north-eastern Tai Po district housed about 4,600 people.

Nearly 40% of the residents were 65 or older, and many of the fire's victims were elderly people.

Thousands of firefighters were deployed to bring the fire under control. One of them, 37-year-old Ho Wai-ho, died during the firefighting operation.

The fire deeply shocked and worried Hong Kong, a densely populated city where many residents live in similar ageing high-rises, and sparked calls for accountability.

articles.title: Netanyahu alleges fraud as Arab parties score record gains — emerge as potential kingmakers
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu alleges Israel's election was "stolen by Arab parties," demanding police investigate as Arab voter turnout hit record levels.
articles.body: TEL AVIV, Israel: Israel's two Arab parties are in a position to have a say in who the country's next prime minister and government will be — but not if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has anything to do with it, after he alleged serious criminal activities took place during voting in the Arab areas of the nation. The two parties were projected to win a combined 19 Knesset seats, according to preliminary results. With both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led right-wing bloc and the opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s centrist bloc falling short of the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Netanyahu wrote on X that Israel’s election had been "stolen by Arab parties that support terrorism and the elimination of the Jewish state," alleging serious criminal offenses, including bribery, threats, violence, forgery and the use of prohibited software to mobilize voters. NETANYAHU GAINS OVERNIGHT AS ISRAEL ELECTION HEADS TOWARD POLITICAL DEADLOCK "The Likud party is transferring to the police, the Shin Bet, and the Central Elections Committee hundreds of testimonies and pieces of evidence regarding election theft in many Arab polling stations," he wrote. He cited allegations of thousands of envelopes containing cash and Ra’am ballot slips, threats and violence against polling station staff, multiple votes cast behind the voting curtain, voting under multiple identities, discrepancies between the number of ballot envelopes and the number of voters, the use of prohibited voter-mobilization software and other offenses. "We demand from the police and the Shin Bet a thorough investigation into the election theft by the Arab parties and the full prosecution of the criminals. We demand from the Central Elections Committee an immediate response to investigate these criminal offenses that have severely damaged the integrity of the elections in Israel and the election results," he added. One Arab political alliance, the Joint List, brings together three parties: Hadash, a predominantly Arab-Jewish left-wing party rooted in Israel’s communist movement, and the Arab nationalist parties Ta’al and Balad. With over 90% of ballots counted, the alliance was projected to win 12 seats. The other Arab party, the United Arab List (Ra’am), led by Mansour Abbas and affiliated with the Southern Branch of the Islamic Movement in Israel, was projected to win seven seats. Arab citizens make up approximately 21% of Israel’s population. Turnout in this election reached a near record high between 75% to 80%. "They are a political force to be reckoned with," Dahlia Scheindlin, a former policy fellow at the Mitvim Institute and a senior analyst at Haaretz, told Fox News Digital. NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE Scheindlin said that Netanyahu framed his campaign around the claim that the opposition is prepared to form a government dependent on Arab parties’ support, which he argues would lead to the establishment of a Palestinian state that would become a terror state and ultimately bring about Israel’s destruction. "This is the most consistent message, and he never stopped saying it, including on election day," she said. Scheindlin said that the issue had become politically sensitive, prompting leading Zionist opposition parties to pledge not to cooperate with the Arab parties. "They have sworn they would not build a coalition that depends on Arab votes, either from within the coalition or from outside it. If they receive any help, they will have to break that promise," she added. It is not inconceivable, though highly unlikely, that Netanyahu could reach out to one of the Arab parties to explore the possibility of cooperation, Scheindlin said. ISRAEL HEADS INTO DEEPLY DIVIDED ELECTION AS OCT. 7 RECKONING LOOMS: WHAT TO KNOW Dr. Arik Rudnitzky, a researcher in the Israel Democracy Institute’s Arab Society in Israel Program, said that Arab parties had historically remained in the opposition and had not joined governing coalitions. During the governments of Yitzhak Rabin and, later, Shimon Peres in the 1990s, Arab parties provided a parliamentary safety net from outside the coalition. This enabled the government to remain in office and complete its term even after it effectively became a minority government amid opposition to the Oslo Accords, as the Haredi Shas party left the government. "Historically, Arab parties were always in the opposition for many reasons. It was quite uncommon to believe Arab parties could [support] the government. It’s a novelty of recent years, plus the fact that their political strength in terms of the number of seats was not as significant as it is today," Rudnitzky said. Demographic changes alone do not explain the Arab parties’ growing political strength, Rudnitzky said; shifting voting patterns have also played a role. "In the past, Arab voters supported both Arab and Jewish parties. In the 1980s and 1990s, approximately half voted for Jewish parties," he continued. Rudnitzky said historical developments, the impact of the Oslo Accords and the entry of new Arab representatives into the Knesset contributed to a gradual shift away from Jewish parties, with more Arab voters turning to Arab parties. "Today, we can say that between 85% and 90% of Arab voters support Arab parties. This is the main reason for their increased political strength," he added. Any support Arab parties might provide to a prospective coalition would come in exchange for political concessions, Rudnitzky said. Their demands would likely include a government decision and a plan to combat crime in Arab communities, as well as a new socioeconomic development plan for the Arab sector involving budget allocations. Ultimately, he said, such arrangements would involve allocating public goods and resources in exchange for political support. "There is no free lunch in politics. Every collaboration, either within a coalition or from the outside, has its political price." TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE Scheindlin noted that while the Joint List would not be invited to join a governing coalition — and its members would not want to do so anyway — Mansour Abbas and his United Arab List have pursued a different, more controversial approach. The party has accepted Israel as a Jewish state and seeks to improve the lives of Arab citizens within that framework, she said. "They are expecting equality as citizens. They accepted Israel’s identity and are willing to work within that framework to improve the lives of their citizens. They are the only ones who have a chance of being invited into a coalition, as they were in 2021," she said. In September, the Central Elections Committee (CEC) voted to disqualify the Joint List and the United Arab list from competing in the Oct. 27 elections. On Oct. 2, Israel’s Supreme Court overturned the CEC’s decisions against both parties. Section 7A of the Basic Law: The Knesset bars candidates who deny Israel’s existence as a Jewish and democratic state, incite to racism, or support the armed struggle of an enemy state or terrorist organization against Israel from participating in Knesset elections. Martin Sherman, founder and executive director of the Israel Institute for Strategic Studies, told Fox News Digital that Arab parties in Israel are essentially illegal and should be barred from participating in elections. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "They have different social agendas, perhaps, but on the political level, they all oppose Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people. One can only hope that politicians in Israel will realize that and that political ambitions and animosity toward Netanyahu will not prevail," he said. One former Israeli diplomat noted the irony and said it was a good teaching moment for those who don't understand the country. "Arab Israelis voted in huge numbers and, according to the exit polls, won more Knesset seats than ever before. That is the answer to the ridiculously ignorant accusation that Israel is a supposed ‘apartheid’ state," Shahar Azani, veteran israeli diplomat and former spokesperson of Israel’s consulate in New York, told Fox News Digital. He added, "Arab citizens are shaping the government and taking part in the Jewish state's democratic celebration, and we welcome it. But with great power comes great responsibility: they must now take the next step and reject the extremist positions some voiced as soon as the results came in, that would alienate them from Israel's Jewish majority."

articles.title: Trump demands Alaska candidates be removed over alleged ballot scheme
articles.summary: A New York Times investigation links Democratic operatives to a namesake candidate in Alaska’s Senate race.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has called for the removal and prosecution of two candidates in Alaska’s Senate race , accusing Democrats of orchestrating a scheme to mislead voters.

Trump’s demand on Wednesday followed a New York Times investigation into efforts by people linked to Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign to recruit candidates who could draw support from Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, including a retired teacher with the same name.

The November 3 vote could help determine control of the US Senate, Congress’s upper chamber.

In Truth Social posts on Wednesday, Trump accused Peltola and Daniel J Sullivan Jr of election fraud and called for both to be removed from the ballot and prosecuted.

He described the alleged operation as “Voter Fraud at the Highest Level” and accused Democrats of lying under oath.

The Times noted that recruiting candidates to split an opponent’s vote – a practice known as ballot stacking – is generally legal and has been used by both parties in Alaska.

The two Sullivans are among four candidates in Alaska’s ranked-choice election.

Voters rank candidates by preference, with votes transferred if a first choice is eliminated. The ballot identifies the sitting senator as an incumbent Republican.

His namesake says he entered the race independently.

The Times reported that the effort began in 2025, when a Peltola aide was asked to identify Alaskans named Dan Sullivan.

Citing interviews and messages, it said Peltola advisers and officials from the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, which supports Democratic Senate candidates, discussed ways to reshape the ballot.

The newspaper identified Democratic operative Jerid Kurtz as a recruiter who approached potential candidates, sometimes under an assumed name.

It also reported that another Democrat withdrew after an approach from Kurtz, opening a place for Republican Gerald Heikes, who said he too had been encouraged to run.

Peltola’s former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, told the Times that Peltola knew about the operation but did not participate directly.

Rios later sought to withdraw her statements and the newspaper said other evidence supported its reporting.

Peltola’s campaign and the Democratic campaign committee denied recruiting candidates. Her campaign said political threats from Washington would not stop her candidacy.

Senator Sullivan accused Peltola of deceiving voters on Fox News on Wednesday.

Recruiting candidates to divide an opponent’s support is generally legal, the Times noted, and both major parties have used such tactics in Alaska.

The state’s Supreme Court upheld the retired teacher’s right to stand in June.

Trump’s Justice Department, the federal government’s legal arm, sued Alaska last week, seeking to delay certification if Senator Sullivan loses and votes for his namesake could have affected the outcome.

Alaska has asked the court to dismiss the case, arguing that it lacks legal grounds.

articles.title: Girl, 8, injured in wolf attack at German zoo
articles.summary: An 8-year-old girl has been hospitalized after sustaining serious injuries in a wolf attack inside a German zoo’s enclosure.
articles.body: An 8-year-old girl has been hospitalized after sustaining serious injuries in a wolf attack inside a German zoo’s enclosure. The girl was with two other children and a staff member when at least one wolf attacked her on Wednesday morning at Johannismühle Wildlife Park, south of Berlin, police said in a statement Wednesday. The facility had been holding a special event for children at the time of the incident, the Associated Press reported, citing Teltow-Fläming district officials. The zookeeper intervened before the two other girls in the Arctic wolf enclosure were attacked, according to AP. The injured girl was airlifted to hospital, while the others appeared unharmed, according to the police, who said they were investigating the incident. The zoo remains closed until at least November 2, according to its website. The attack is the latest in a string of incidents involving captive animals that have hit headlines in recent months. A zookeeper in the Netherlands died on Tuesday after being attacked by a leopard three days earlier at the safari park where she worked. Earlier this month, a man in the UK was killed by a tiger after entering the animal’s enclosure at a wildlife park. In September, a tiger handler linked to “Tiger King” Joe Exotic was killed by one of the big cats at the Oklahoma preserve where he worked. Meanwhile, a wolf bit a woman in a shopping area in Hamburg earlier this year, AP reported, citing authorities, in what’s believed to be the first such attack since wolves returned to Germany in 1998. This story has been updated.

articles.title: This busy Tokyo neighborhood draws thousands of Halloween visitors. Some locals have had enough of the party
articles.summary: Within just a few years, Halloween in Tokyo’s Shibuya neighborhood has gone from organized community event to week-long headache.
articles.body: More than 500,000 people march, walk, skateboard and dance across Shibuya Crossing every day. As the world’s busiest and most famous intersection, it’s an essential Tokyo tourist stop. Many places around the world would love to have a “must visit” destination of this cachet. But Shibuya, one of the city’s most popular neighborhoods, is not so sure it wants to be one of them. Amid complaints of too many tourists and bad behavior, which have led to clashes between residents and visitors, Shibuya’s local government has been trying to change the district’s fashionable reputation. The neighborhood has long been considered the ultimate spot for young people to celebrate Halloween in Japan. In the early 2010s, Shibuya became popular with young families whose kids wanted to dress up in cute costumes. But adults wanted to get in on the fun, too. In 2017, the neighborhood actively promoted “ShibuHallo” as a community event. Shibuya’s central location and popularity with foreigners — it has more than 1,000 registered hotels and other accommodations — meant the party got bigger every year. Now, a decade after “ShibuHallo,” many Shibuya locals want to put the genie back in the bottle. Tokyo is made up of 23 smaller cities, or wards, each with its own leaders, rules and regulations. Ken Hasebe has been the mayor of Shibuya since 2015, and Halloween celebrations have become a bête noire of his administration. This year, Shibuya isn’t pushing ShibuHallo. They’re promoting a different slogan aimed at preventing public disturbances: “Goodbye Bad Halloween.” From novelty to nuisance After Japan reopened post-pandemic, tourism surged — and hasn’t stopped. Mount Fuji’s hiking trails, Niseko’s ski slopes, and Nara’s deer park all began to sag under the weight of overtourism. In 2025, Japan welcomed more than 40 million foreign visitors — about five times as many as in 2012. Amid the increased number of travelers, cultural clashes and misunderstandings have grown more common. For example, visitors to Kyoto’s historic Gion neighborhood were so often seen chasing, harassing, and photographing the city’s famous geishas that locals coined the term “geisha paparazzi.” The city put up signage in multiple languages asking tourists to behave themselves around the women, but not everyone paid heed. Some residents took matters into their own hands, chasing away badly behaved visitors or blocking off private roads. In the capital, though, it’s Halloween, a holiday associated with all things spooky and scary, that has become a real-life nightmare. During Hasebe’s tenure as mayor, Shibuya City’s Halloween celebration has gone from being a neighborhood gathering to an international event. With that came all kinds of new problems: public urination, noise complaints, broken bottles in the street and building damage, among others. In 2018, Hasebe welcomed visitors to the area but urged them to enjoy Halloween without causing inconvenience to others. Although there were hiccups along the way, including a handful of arrests, it seemed like Shibuya City’s polite requests might work to balance a love of dressing up and having fun with a respect for one’s neighbors. But on October 29, 2022, the stakes became much higher. A tragedy next door Two days before Halloween 2022, celebrations were in full swing in Itaewon, the hipster-filled neighborhood in Seoul, South Korea. Some 100,000 people descended on the neighborhood, causing human traffic jams in the narrow streets. Then, tragedy struck — as more and more revelers tried to cram into a popular alleyway, it became a pressure point. People began to collapse, and without a way to quickly exit they began to pile up on top of each other. Some suffocated. Others were crushed. In all, 154 people — mostly Koreans in their 20s and 30s – died that night. The Itaewon news sent shockwaves around the world. Other cities began to wonder if a similar disaster could happen in their own streets. In Shibuya, Halloween festivities were already a nuisance — but now, officials realized there was more to worry about than empty bottles and loud music. Hasebe wrote a public note expressing his condolences for the Itaewon tragedy, adding, “the crowdedness around Shibuya station on the weekend makes us worry that a similar accident might happen in Shibuya, too.” In addition, the mayor made public statements asking people not to come to Shibuya for Halloween. While about 15,000 people still showed up in 2023, it was significantly lower than the crowds of 60,000 or so in previous years. In 2024, crowds were about 20,000. Hasebe estimates that 70-80% of them are international travelers. Over the years, the government has made incremental changes during Halloween week, such as putting up fences around the statue of the famously loyal dog Hachiko — which often has lines of visitors waiting to snap selfies — and asking local shops not to sell alcohol. This year is no exception, with extra security guards set to be stationed at 10 locations around Shibuya during the Halloween weekend. But some Shibuya business owners say the Halloween restrictions hurt them financially. Others complain that they face more issues from local law enforcement than they do from would-be partiers. One izakaya owner told CNN, “Early in the evening there are more police vehicles and officers than people in costume. Police vehicles line up in front of the restaurant, making it impossible to park delivery vehicles.” She asked that her name not be used because she feared repercussions against her business. She adds that her regulars, who are Shibuya office workers, tend to go home early on Halloween to avoid the chaos. She also said that her restaurant — which, while still in the neighborhood, is off the main drag — has “never” been harmed by Halloween partying. For her, the biggest challenge is navigating the crowds in order to make it to the Shibuya Station and not miss the last train of the night, which departs around midnight. Some feel the restrictions don’t go far enough. Tatsuji Suzuki, chairman of the busy Center Gai shopping street, says that while there are more rules in place, such as a 2,000 yen ($13) fine for littering, “there are no penalties.” Without rigorous enforcement, he says, there’s no reason for people to change their behavior. Rather than expect Shibuya City to help, Suzuki says he and his fellow association members decided to work together. “The area once had poor public safety and few rules. Fearing the shopping street would stop functioning if visitors stayed away, the association took action. Because the shopping street acted first, the ward joined in, creating a united front to protect the area.” Now, street cleaning on Center Gai happens every day, rain or shine, and a crime-prevention unit prowls the area. Shibuya has also closed off some public toilets and changing areas in the train station so they can’t be overtaken by partiers getting into their costumes. All-caps posters plastered around the district blare NO LOITERING and NO OBSTRUCTING. For Suzuki, the ultimate goal would be turning October 31 back into just another regular day on the calendar. He tells CNN that Halloween has already begun to fall back out of favor with local Japanese, with fewer people getting into the spirit every year. “It’s reached the point where people feel embarrassed to dress up.” Mayor Hasebe, whose annual Halloween campaigns focus on asking people to mind their manners, suggests an alternative: Celebrate indoors.

articles.title: Elon Musk to everyone: ‘Saving money for the distant future is pointless’; the reason is …
articles.summary: Elon Musk has once again predicted a future of abundance where money will become redundant.
articles.body: Elon Musk has once again predicted a future of abundance where money will become redundant. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), the tech billionaire wrote: “Saving money for the distant future is pointless” in the “super intelligent abundance” driven by AI. Elon Musk’s post responded to a user's lighthearted justification for questionable spending amid expectations of rapid future prosperity. “Justifying each of my questionable financial decisions with the fact that we’re headed towards a future of abundance,” X user @battleangelviv said adding “Don’t be like, totally reckless, but also most of it won’t matter in a few years anyway”.Not a firstThis is not the fist time that Elon Musk predicted a future without money. During an interview with Peter Diamandis earlier this year, an entrepreneur and executive chairman of the XPrize Foundation (via Fortune), Musk laid out a “moonshot” vision of a future where human labour is optional and currency no longer exists.Elon Musk believes that AI robots will change global economics. “AI and robots are going to make so much stuff and provide so many services that they’ll run out of things to do for humans,” Musk said. In Musk's view, this automated abundance will lead to a massive economic shift wherein the volume of goods and services produced by robots will far outpace the actual supply of money, causing retail prices to plummet toward zero.He also said that since robot labor will be cheap and continuous, production costs will practically disappear. Without the need to pay human workers to generate supply, the traditional need for money falls apart.“I think money will stop being relevant at some point in the future,” Musk stated bluntly.Diamandis was quick to point out the contradiction between Musk’s words and his wealth. “So just as you’re becoming a multi-trillionaire, money starts to have less value?” Diamandis asked then. To this, Musk replied: “Yeah, pretty much.”Elon Musk proposes universal high incomeIt must be noted that Elon Musk has previously advocated for a system of “universal high income” to ensure citizens can access this automated abundance. In April, he spoke about what he called “Universal HIGH INCOME,” suggesting that federal government checks could help people cope with large-scale unemployment driven by AI and robotics. He argued that as AI increases productivity, the supply of goods and services could grow faster than the money supply, making such payments sustainable.“Universal HIGH INCOME via checks issued by the Federal government is the best way to deal with unemployment caused by AI,” Elon Musk wrote adding “AI/robotics will produce goods & services far in excess of the increase in the money supply, so there will not be inflation”.You use AI every day. articles.title: Chaos on camera: Armenia MPs trade blows as parliament erupts into mass brawl
articles.summary: A heated exchange over a controversial election promise descended into a mass brawl in Armenia’s parliament on Wednesday, with lawmakers from the ruling
articles.body: A heated exchange over a controversial election promise descended into a mass brawl in Armenia’s parliament on Wednesday, with lawmakers from the ruling party and the opposition trading punches and kicks in a clash broadcast live.The incident took place on Thursday during a debate on the election of a member of the Audit Chamber, after ruling Civil Contract party MP Taron Chakhoyan referred to a pre-election remark by a relative of opposition leader Narek Karapetyan. The remark concerned a proposal to establish a separate “ministry to satisfy women” if the opposition came to power.According to Armenian news agency Armenpress, Chakhoyan reminded Karapetyan that his cousin had yet to apologise for the statement. Karapetyan, who leads the opposition Strong Armenia faction, initially responded from his seat before approaching the podium, triggering a physical confrontation.The verbal altercation escalated into a full-scale fight, with lawmakers using their fists and feet. The brawl reportedly spilled into the parliamentary corridor, where security personnel and fellow MPs struggled to separate those involved. Obscene language was also heard during the confrontation.Parliament Speaker Ruben Rubinyan later held Karapetyan primarily responsible for the incident, saying he had reviewed footage of the exchange during the break and found no offensive remarks in Chakhoyan’s speech.“Mr. Karapetyan, you failed to control your emotions, made offensive remarks from your seat, and then stood up and attempted to hit Taron Chakhoyan,” Rubinyan said, according to Armenpress. He added that opposition MP Garnik Davtyan had struck Chakhoyan once the brawl began.Rubinyan also said he had deliberately allowed the live broadcast to continue so the public could see what was happening inside parliament.An ambulance arrived at the parliamentary building following the clash. articles.title: Bass fishing's biggest stars battle for record $1.25 million payday in historic Nashville showdown
articles.summary: Sixty of the best pro bass anglers clash on Old Hickory Lake as Jacob Wheeler says winning The Champions would top his entire decorated career.
articles.body: Sixty of the best professional bass anglers in the world. Three days of competition. One lake. And a whopping $1.25 million payday waiting for whoever comes out on top. The biggest names in professional bass fishing have descended on Middle Tennessee for the inaugural The Champions tournament, where a record $3.25 million purse is up for grabs on Old Hickory Lake. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS But this isn't just about the money. For the first time ever, 30 of the top anglers from the Bassmaster Elite Series will go head-to-head with 30 of Major League Fishing's (MLF) Bass Pro Tour stars in a tournament designed to settle one of the sport's biggest debates: Who's really the best? And according to MLF superstar Jacob Wheeler, winning this one would mean more than just about anything else he's accomplished in his decorated career. "It would have to be number one," Wheeler told OutKick OutDoors during Wednesday's Media Day in Nashville. "This is like in football, you have an AFC championship and an NFC championship, and basically we never compete against the other league, right?" he explained. "So now for us to come together and compete under one roof, one tournament here in Nashville ... it would have the most meaning." "The money's one thing, and that's great, but it's the meaning of being the best for that year." The competition begins Thursday at 7:30 a.m. CT, with the anglers divided into Team Stars (Bassmaster) and Team Stripes (MLF). They'll compete for team bragging rights over the first two days, with the top 15 individual anglers advancing to Saturday's championship round. Weights will reset for the final day, when one angler will walk away with the biggest first-place payout in bass fishing history. And just to make things interesting, two amateur anglers — Eric Giessing of Missouri and Kyle Carr of Texas — earned their spots through a sweepstakes and will compete alongside the pros. The old guard isn't handing anything over While the two circuits are coming together for a historic event, that doesn't mean there isn't a little friendly competition brewing. Team Stripes captain Zack Birge believes his squad has an advantage over the Bassmaster youngsters. And it has a lot to do with experience. "I just feel like the other side has a lot of young, talented guys," Birge told OutKick OutDoors. "We have a lot of middle-aged guys." So, basically, he's calling his teammates old? "Yeah, basically," Birge laughed. BASSMASTER PRO COOPER GALLANT SAYS BASS FISHING IS ACTUALLY MORE FUN WITHOUT LIVESCOPE SONAR But his argument is that the more experienced anglers have a deeper arsenal of traditional fishing techniques to fall back on, while some of their younger competitors are more accustomed to relying on electronics. "I feel like that gives us an advantage here, especially on a tough one," he said. And Wheeler, for one, agrees with his captain. "We call them the OGs," Wheeler said of the veterans on Team Stripes. "That experience definitely does play a role." Of course, the young guns aren't exactly lacking confidence. Bassmaster Angler of the Year Trey McKinney acknowledged that there's a target on his back after his remarkable 2026 season. But he's not particularly worried about it. "We're all equal competitors," McKinney said. "We're all buddies and friends ... but when we get out on the water, we put our hard hats on, and that's when we go to work." Old Hickory isn't making things easy As if battling the best anglers in the world for a life-changing amount of money weren't stressful enough, Old Hickory Lake has decided not to cooperate. The notoriously challenging fishery has already tested the competitors during practice, with low water levels and little current making the bass difficult to locate. "It's a grind, and you got to stay at it 100%," McKinney said. In fact, the 21-year-old believes the difficult conditions could create an opportunity for a surprise winner — potentially even one of the two amateur competitors. "This is the one tournament that I think the Average Joes could literally win," McKinney said, explaining that the unpredictable fishing could level the playing field. Another wrinkle? Forward-facing sonar. Anglers must choose whether to use the technology Thursday or Friday, but not both days. On Championship Saturday, they'll be permitted to use it for only half of the competition. MLF pro Drew Gill, known for being a LiveScope expert, believes those restrictions could have an enormous impact on the final results. "When it comes down to Saturday, that day where we're all fishing for the win, that three hours is going to shake things up because this lake is definitely a tremendous hurdle," Gill told OutKick OutDoors. "That intel from seeing underwater is just so darn valuable, even when you shut it off," he added. With so much money on the line, even the most seasoned pros will have to find a way to manage their emotions. Wheeler believes that could ultimately separate the winner from everybody else. "The key is you have to sort of control your emotion. And it's hard to do in an event this big," he said. "But that's what the best do in big moments." For McKinney, a victory would mean more than a trophy and a trip to the bank. "When you're talking retirement-status money that you're fishing for," he said, the stakes are impossible to ignore. And if he does happen to pocket that $1.25 million? SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER "First thing I'm doing, heading to the beach," McKinney said. "And I'm going to sit there with my toes in the sand for about a week and a half or more." After that, he'll worry about investing. articles.title: Trump’s crony diplomacy is marginalizing Marco Rubio
articles.summary: Undercutting the secretary of state’s role, Trump has recast U.S. diplomacy in his own image — personalized, transactional, overbearing and opaque.
articles.body:
Outsourcing high-stakes diplomacy to family members and business associates would provoke public outrage in most democracies. President Trump, however, has normalized the practice.

In this model of crony diplomacy, personal loyalty, private gain and informal networks routinely override institutional processes and the national interest, while accountability diminishes.

Against this backdrop, it may scarcely be surprising that Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s recent overseas travels have skirted the world’s main hot spots. Rubio’s latest travels have taken him to Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Iceland, Greece, Portugal and, most recently, Uzbekistan and India.

Trump, instead of relying on Rubio and the professional diplomatic corps, has repeatedly turned to his son-in-law, Jared Kushner, and business partner Steve Witkoff — a Manhattan real-estate figure — to spearhead high-stakes negotiations on Ukraine, Russia, Gaza and Iran. Both men entered their roles as “ special envoys ” for peace with no prior diplomatic experience. Both also have glaring conflicts of interest .

Rubio’s travel schedule heavily favors lower-risk regions while avoiding the main theaters of global conflict. Critics speculate that he is doing this deliberately to safeguard his own political future. By keeping his distance from the Trump administration’s messiest and most volatile foreign-policy crises, including his muddled China policy , Rubio stays clear of issues that could end badly.

Rubio may have calculated that his long-term career — potentially including a presidential run in 2028 — is best served by bypassing the administration’s core foreign-policy minefields .

Rubio, however, has remained the administration’s point man on Venezuela and Cuba. Neither Venezuela nor Cuba, though, has done much to burnish his record.

The Trump administration’s strategy since January of strangling Cuba has created a severe humanitarian crisis on the island without bringing about regime change. Meanwhile, the success of the U.S. military operation in Venezuela in capturing the country’s sitting president only emboldened Trump’s war on Iran, which has turned into a politically costly fiasco for him. Even as Venezuelans bristle over the U.S. takeover of their country’s oil wealth, Trump boasted : “We’ve taken out so much oil in Venezuela, we paid for the cost of the war [on Iran] about 25 times over.”

Venezuela’s oil-export revenues are deposited directly into accounts controlled by the U.S. Treasury, with Rubio effectively overseeing both its exports and finances, including when, how much and for what purposes funds are released to Caracas. This relationship has frequently been described as akin to a “weekly allowance” for approved humanitarian or infrastructure purposes. From afar, Rubio effectively runs Venezuela in neocolonial fashion.

Expanding Venezuela’s oil exports was one of the key objectives behind Rubio’s recent trip to India, where he paid a private visit to the world’s largest oil-refining complex in Jamnagar.

Refining Venezuela’s high-sulfur, ultra-heavy crude is significantly more energy-intensive, carbon-intensive and time-consuming than refining light, sweet crude. While light, sweet crude yields relatively high proportions of gasoline and diesel through atmospheric distillation, heavy crude demands extensive, multistage conversion to produce marketable products. Still, the Jamnagar refining complex has emerged as a leading buyer and processor of U.S.-controlled Venezuelan heavy crude.

With a crude-processing capacity of about 1.4 million barrels per day, Jamnagar stands out globally as one of the few hyper-complex private export hubs capable of processing different crude varieties into ultra-clean, Euro VI-compliant fuels on an enormous scale.

Calling India, the world’s third-largest oil importer , a “refining superpower,” Rubio pitched greater purchases of Venezuelan crude for processing at Jamnagar to help ease a global diesel crunch and other refined-fuel shortages. Jamnagar makes India a leading global exporter of diesel and other refined fuels, supplying markets across Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas. Jamnagar’s refined-product exports dwarf those of individual refineries elsewhere, including in the U.S.

Owned by Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries, the complex features a dedicated export-only facility within a Special Economic Zone, allowing it to serve as a crucial swing supplier to international markets. That Rubio’s visit followed Elon Musk’s public attacks on Ambani, whom he mockingly styled “Prime Minister Ambani,” illustrated the blurring line between commercial rivalry, personal patronage and official diplomacy in Trump’s Washington.

India, seeking energy resilience through diversification, is unlikely to substantially increase Venezuelan oil imports, which in any case come with higher transportation and marine-insurance costs. Nor are Indian firms likely to accept Rubio’s proposal that they invest directly in restoring Venezuela’s dilapidated oil fields under American oversight, given the financial losses the companies have suffered from past U.S. policy reversals.

With political ties with New Delhi under pressure largely because of Trump’s policies, Rubio’s India visit sought to shift the focus toward energy security and corporate partnerships. By limiting his itinerary to India’s commercial capital, Mumbai, and the Jamnagar complex, Rubio emphasized pragmatic cooperation over diplomatic friction.

Rubio’s India visit, however, exemplified the limits of what a fragmented foreign policy can deliver in an era of American crony diplomacy.

Diplomacy is not merely deal-making , as Trump seems to believe. Since Trump’s return to office, U.S. diplomacy in the Middle East, for example, has increasingly reflected personal and commercial priorities. Kushner’s “New Gaza” proposal , unveiled at Davos, has been widely criticized as “real estate diplomacy” — a plan that treats large-scale devastation as a commercial opportunity.

Undercutting the secretary of state’s role, Trump has recast U.S. diplomacy in his own image — personalized, transactional, overbearing and opaque.

The result is a U.S. that is less credible, less trusted and ultimately less effective on the world stage.

Brahma Chellaney is the author of nine books, including the award-winning “Water: Asia’s New Battleground. “

articles.title: HRTC to run 266 special buses for Diwali
articles.summary: HRTC will run 266 special buses from Delhi, Chandigarh and Baddi to Himachal destinations on Nov 6-7 for Diwali; minimum services on Nov 8.
articles.body: Shimla: The Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) will operate 266 special buses from Delhi, Chandigarh and Baddi to various destinations in Himachal Pradesh on Nov 6 and 7 to facilitate the return of people home for Diwali, deputy chief minister Mukesh Agnihotri said on Thursday.Of the total services, 134 buses will operate on Nov 6 and 132 on Nov 7. On Nov 6, 42 buses will depart from Delhi, 69 from Chandigarh and 23 from Baddi. On Nov 7, HRTC will run 49 buses from Delhi, 63 from Chandigarh and 20 from Baddi. Preparations are underway to ensure convenient travel for passengers during the festive rush. Agnihotri said the special services had been planned to help people living and working outside the state celebrate Diwali with their families. He added that HRTC would maintain minimum bus services on Diwali, which falls on Nov 8. Services on important routes, including Delhi and Chandigarh, would continue as required, while buses within Himachal Pradesh would operate until 4 pm.
